sources.title: BNaR digitized archival inventory: Iurghiceni documents, 1591–1592, 1611 and 1619; separate 1599 court judgment
supports: 1547 Iurghiceni Cican/Cicican record in same archival series
1599 separate Ieremia Movilă court judgment requiring independent inspection
1611: Frim son of Bilan sells his Iurghiceni ocină to his nephew Costinovici
1611 I/18: the BNaR inventory explicitly calls Costinovici a vistier (treasurer/treasury official), not merely a person bearing the name Costinovici
sources.independence: Primary archival catalogue; catalogue adjacency does not establish person or family continuity. Individual document contents must be inspected.
sources.notes: BNaR inventory establishes I/14 (1591–1592) as a genuine Iurghiceni transaction: Ștefan son of Cătrîna, grandson of priest Gavril, sells his Iurghiceni share from the Băsărăbești side to his cousin Obrejie, son of Agafia and grandson of priest Gavril, for 40 zlotys. The verso is annotated 'Cost. Paladi hatm.' This is an archival annotation/verso note, not evidence that the 1591–1592 transaction was authored by the later Constantin Paladi. The same caution applies to later BNaR items carrying a Paladi verso/author field: chronology must come from the underlying document, not the later annotation alone.

sources.title: Documente privind istoria României, A. Moldova, veacul XVII, vol. IV (1616–1620)
sources.source_type: scholarly documentary edition / published historical record index
supports: 1619 June 20: Costin and Lupu vistiernici receive confirmation of an Iurghiceni holding bought from Iosif, son of Vasile Cergas, for 46 talers
1619 June 20: Costin vistiernicel from Iurghiceni receives confirmation of an Iurghiceni holding bought from Frimu son of Bilan for 46 silver talers
1620 July 22: Gaspar confirms Costin of Iurghiceni in possession of his holding
sources.independence: Scholarly documentary edition; use original archival documents for final person-level claims where available.
sources.notes: The 1619 edition contains multiple closely dated Costin formulations: Costin and Lupu vistiernici in one transaction, and Costin vistiernicel from Iurghiceni in the Frimu son of Bilan transaction. This must be resolved from the underlying documents before treating every Costin reference as one individual.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A Moldova, vol. XXI (1632–1633): Iurghiceni Costin and local ownership records

17 April 1632: Iurghiceni local witnesses include Băsărab, Miron, Onciul, Obrejie, Andronic and Vasile Văsian
17 April 1632: Andronic and Irimia pledge their Iurghiceni holding
sources.independence: Scholarly documentary edition reproducing/transcribing archival records; useful for tracing later Iurghiceni property context, but does not establish a Cican connection.

sources.title: Documente privind istoria României A Moldova, 1384–1625: Index de nume de persoane (1995)
supports: Index entry identifies Bilan as father of Frim from Iurghiceni, with a 1619 reference in Documente privind istoria României, A Moldova, vol. IV
sources.independence: Scholarly index to the documentary edition; secondary index evidence confirming the named relationship and locality, to be checked against the underlying document.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. V (1621–1625), doc. 129 — Gligorie and his brother Costin of Iurghiceni
supports: 6 January 1622: Ștefan Tomșa confirms Gligorie and his brother Costin, vistiernicei from Iurghiceni, their jointly purchased share of Arvasia, daughter of Marco, granddaughter of Gage, bought from Umbrar vataf of Rădeni for 35 silver talers
sources.independence: Scholarly edition of the documentary record; primary-document transcription.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXI (1632–1633), doc. 22 — Gavril and Gligorie, sons of Palaghia, Iurghiceni
supports: 17 April 1632: Gavril and his brother Gligorie, sons of Palaghia and grandchildren of Miron, sell their Iurghiceni hereditary holding to Iachim Bandur
sources.independence: Primary-document transcription in a scholarly edition.
sources.notes: The 17 April 1632 original says Gavril and his brother Gligorie, sons of Palaghia and grandsons of Miron, sold their hereditary holding from the fourth part of Iurghiceni. The phrase also refers to their share being selected from the shares of 'other brothers', showing that the sibling group was larger than the two named here. This means the 1622 Gligorie's brother Costin cannot be ruled out solely because Costin is not named in the 1632 sale; however, the 1632 document does not identify Costin as a son of Palaghia.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. V (1621–1625): 6 January 1622 paired Costin–Grigore/Gligorie records
supports: 6 January 1622: one entry identifies Grigore and Costin vistiernicel from Iurghiceni in a Rădeni holding purchased from Umbrar
6 January 1622, doc. 129: Ștefan Tomșa confirms Gligorie and his brother Costin vistiernicei from Iurghiceni in the same Rădeni/Umbrar purchase context
sources.independence: Scholarly documentary edition. The paired entries provide a strong textual variant/identity clue for Grigore/Gligorie, subject to checking the printed pagination and original documents.

sources.title: BNaR finding aids: later Iurghiceni records involving Costin; Vasco–Costin–Iacob
supports: BNaR item 3357: multiple Iurghiceni villagers attest to Costin's holding
BNaR item 3444 (inventory cotă I/135): 'Părțile de moșie din Iurghiceni ale fraților Vasco, Costin, Iacob, ce trebuie să se aleagă…'; the verso is noted as 'Constantin Paladi hatman'
BNaR item 3445: Iurghiceni shares from the Băsărăbești side
sources.independence: Archival finding aid; individual undated entries require recovery of the underlying scans before chronological placement.
sources.notes: Important chronological correction: item 3444 is NOT safe to use as evidence for the 1611–1632 Costin. BNaR marks its date as [s.d.] and the verso names Constantin Paladi hatman. Independent historical literature identifies hatman Constantin Paladi as a late-18th/early-19th-century figure who died in 1831. Therefore item 3444 is currently a much later finding aid/document and must be kept separate from the 17th-century Costin until its exact date and provenance are established. Item 3357 also requires recovery and dating before use.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXV (1639–1640), docs. 173 and 187 — Obrejie and the Băsărăbești share of Iurghiceni
supports: 15 July 1639: Irina, daughter of Mărica Nehoe and granddaughter of Băsărabă, and Niță vătaf sell to Obrejie, son of Agahia and nephew of priest Gavril, their Iurghiceni share from the Băsărăbești family for 50 zlotys
22 July 1639: Vasile son of Andrieca and Costantin son of Ana, grandsons of Borcea, sell to Obreje, son of Agahia, their Iurghiceni share from the Băsărăbești family for 35 zlotys
sources.independence: Scholarly edition of primary documentary records.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXIII (1637–1638), doc. 110 — two Obrejie identities at Iurghiceni
supports: 26 May 1637: Obrejie of Iurghiceni, son of Miron, appears with other Iurghiceni răzeși in a collective testimony
26 May 1637: a separate Obrejie, son of Lupu, is also named from Iurghiceni in the same record
1637 demonstrates that multiple distinct Obrejie identities existed at Iurghiceni
sources.independence: Scholarly edition of primary documentary record.
sources.notes: This source is important for deduplication. The 1637 record explicitly distinguishes Obrejie son of Miron from Obrejie son of Lupu. Neither is identified as the son of Agahia/Agafia. Therefore the 1639 Obrejie son of Agahia should not be merged with either 1637 Obrejie without additional evidence.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXVII (1643–1644), doc. 459 — Miron of Iurghiceni and deceased son Obrejie
supports: 28 November 1644: Miron of Iurghiceni donates his share of Iurghiceni for the soul of his deceased son Obrejie
The record identifies a distinct Miron–Obrejie parent-child relationship at Iurghiceni in 1644
sources.independence: Scholarly edition of a primary documentary record.
sources.notes: This Obrejie is not automatically the 1639 Obrejie son of Agahia, nor the 1637 Obrejie son of Miron or son of Lupu. The record instead establishes a separate Miron–Obrejie family clue requiring identity comparison.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXVIII (1645–1646), doc. 43 — Obrejie and Miron of Iurghiceni
supports: 31 March 1645: Obrejie and Miron of Iurghiceni appear as named local witnesses to the transfer of a Iurghiceni holding by Pavăl Băzarca and Cozma Duma
The record places Obrejie and Miron together in the same Iurghiceni community in 1645
sources.independence: Scholarly edition of a primary documentary record.
sources.notes: This record does not give Obrejie's patronymic and therefore cannot by itself identify him as the 1639 Obrejie son of Agahia or the deceased son of Miron in the 1644 record. It is useful as a chronological/community continuity marker only.

sources.title: Documenta Romaniae Historica A. Moldova, vol. XXIV (1637–1638), doc. 410 — Iurghiceni Doșcești branch and Agafia
supports: 14 July 1638: Iachim Bandur sells to Dumitrașco Buhuş an Iurghiceni holding purchased from Petrea Băltag
The prior title is traced to Ion and Constantin, sons of Sidor and Agafia, in the upper half of Iurghiceni, Doșcești side
Agafia is independently documented in the Iurghiceni property network in 1638
sources.independence: Scholarly edition of a primary documentary record.
sources.notes: Identity-control evidence. The Agafia in this 1638 Doșcești-side title chain is not to be equated with the Agafia/Agahia named as Obrejie's parent in the 1591–1592 and 1639 Băsărăbești-side records without explicit kinship or property evidence.

sources.title: Forebears — Cican surname distribution and estimated incidence
supports: External estimate of approximately 399 Cican surname bearers
Country distribution reported by the database
Distinction between surname and forename uses in its database
sources.independence: External aggregated surname database; useful as a benchmark and research lead, not treated as a census or authoritative population count.
sources.notes: The current page reports approximately 399 people bearing the surname, with 212 in Romania, 148 in Turkey, 17 in the United States, 9 in Indonesia, 7 in India, and 1 each in Brazil, Cyprus, England, Peru and Slovenia; it separately reports Çiçan and notes that Cican may also occur as a forename. HOUSE OF CICAN records these figures as an external estimate to audit rather than as established fact. Internal consistency check: the visible country incidence values listed on the current page sum to 398, while the headline says approximately 399 and the page says Cican occurs in 11 countries (Romania plus 10 others), whereas the visible table in the captured result lists Romania plus 9 other countries. HOUSE OF CICAN records this discrepancy for verification rather than attempting to reconcile it by assumption.

sources.title: Românul, 1914 — report on the burning of Nicolae Cican's house in Corcea
sources.publisher: Românul / Biblioteca Centrală Universitară Cluj digital collection
supports: Nicolae Cican in Corcea in March 1914
contemporary report that his house was burned and he escaped alive
historical context for his 1914 return and public activity

sources.title: Țara lui Mircea, 15 October 1936 — bust of nationalist fighter Nicolae Cicani
sources.independence: Bibliographic secondary source pointing to a 1936 periodical item; original issue should be recovered for full context.
sources.notes: The bibliography records a bust of nationalist fighter Nicolae Cicani from the commune of Frașari, published in Țara lui Mircea, year 2, no. 40, 15 October 1936. It is not merged with Nicolae Cican without identity evidence.

sources.title: România Nouă, 20 February 1918 — death of sub-lieutenant Nicolae Cican in Chișinău
sources.publisher: România Nouă / Biblioteca Centrală Universitară Cluj digital collection
sources.independence: Contemporary newspaper report; strongest current documentary evidence for exact death date/place and military rank, pending military personnel/casualty record.
sources.notes: Issue dated 20 February 1918 states that sub-lieutenant Nicolae Cican, a Romanian from Macedonia, died suddenly in Chișinău the previous day and that his funeral would occur that afternoon.

sources.title: Un popor care se stinge, 1915 — Nicolae Cican and Spiru Cican in Corcea
supports: Nicolae Cican as a banker in Corcea
Nicolae Cican's burned house and signed testimony
Spiru Cican as Nicolae's brother and tenant
sources.independence: Contemporary published testimony/report; strong identity-context evidence, but exact publication provenance and underlying original testimony should be documented further.
sources.notes: The source reproduces Nicolae Cican's signed statement after his house was burned, identifies him as a banker, and explicitly states that Spiru Cican was his brother and tenant. This is high-value bridge evidence for the Nicolae/Spiru cluster and should be kept distinct from any unsupported relationship among other 1903 Cicans.

sources.title: Nicolae Cican — Initiator and Founder of the Society Farsarotul
supports: Nicolae Cican's large family with many brothers and sisters
sources.independence: Institutional historical biography attributed to Nick Balamaci Sr., Secretary of the Society Farsarotul, with article dated 1942 and republished in the 1987 newsletter.
sources.notes: The biography states that Nicolae Cican graduated from the Romanian high school in Monastir and emigrated to America around the turn of the century. It also says he had many brothers and sisters, but does not name them. This is a family-size lead, not proof that any other Cican record is his sibling.
